newsitem.title: UK: WILLIS TO SELL MEMBERS AGENT TO MANAGEMENT.
newsitem.headline: WILLIS TO SELL MEMBERS AGENT TO MANAGEMENT.

text.p: British insurance broker Willis Corroon Group Plc said on Wednesday it had signed a letter of intent with the management Willis Faber & Dumas (Agencies) Limited for the sale to them of its interest.
The transaction is subject to Lloyd's approval and Willis said further details will be announced in due course.
Agencies, a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Group, is a Lloyd's members' agent.

It provides advice and management to 689 individual Names - the traditional backers of the Lloyd's insurance market - and to two corporate capital vehicles, which in aggregate provide some 430 million pounds ($704.3 million) of underwriting capacity.
Willis chairman John Reeve said the move was part of the group's strategy to focus resources in areas where it could establish leadership positions.
Willis is concentrating on its core risk management and broking business.
"This approach, combined with current and anticipated changes in the nature of the Lloyd's market, makes continued ownership of our Lloyd's agency business inappropriate," said Reeve.

"The transfer of this business to its management, combined with our strategic alliance with Agencies, provides the best means of redeploying our resources whilst maintaining continuity with the Names that we have been privileged to represent.
James Sinclair, Managing Director of Agencies, said it would enable them to develop the company for the benefit of Names and take full advantage of the opportunities which the new Lloyd's presents.
The group is to maintain a strategic alliance with Willis.
Willis is to keep profit commission for the 1994, 1995, 1996 open years and half the profit commission for 1997. ($ = 0.610 British Pounds)
